pending_commit.commit_message: UPSTREAM: drm/rockchip: remove redundant statement The call to arm_iommu_detach_device() on the previous line sets dev->archdata.mapping to NULL so this call is always a no-op. BUG=chrome-os-partner:53565 TEST=Test eDP on rk3288-minnie Change-Id: I60d3fd5ffd400d954e41cdfbee782cd59fe606af Signed-off-by: John Keeping <john@metanate.com> Signed-off-by: Douglas Anderson <dianders@chromium.org> (cherry picked from git://people.freedesktop.org/~airlied/linux drm-next commit aa1ac27f48de0ed94d5a104e15b5ab62b5deb236) Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/346300

UPSTREAM: drm/rockchip: don't leak iommu mapping arm_iommu_attach_device() takes its own reference to the mapping we give it. Since we do not keep a reference to the mapping ourselves, we must release it before returning. Also fix the error path, which fails to release the mapping if it has called arm_iommu_detach_device() since that clears archdata.mapping. BUG=chrome-os-partner:53565 TEST=Test eDP on rk3288-minnie Change-Id: I1af9a67bc4ef91891806e4fcd8ba79e3241b19a9 Signed-off-by: John Keeping <john@metanate.com> Signed-off-by: Douglas Anderson <dianders@chromium.org> (cherry picked from git://people.freedesktop.org/~airlied/linux drm-next commit 69b007968e7519cf1e44920f4578054c9e0fbdc3) Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/346301

UPSTREAM: drm/rockchip: vop: fix iommu crash with async atomic After async atomic_commit callback, drm_atomic_clean_old_fb will clean all old fb, but because async, the old fb may be also on the vop hardware, dma will access the old fb buffer, clean old fb will cause iommu page fault. Reference the fb and unreference it when the fb actuall swap out from vop hardware. BUG=chrome-os-partner:53565 TEST=Test eDP on rk3288-minnie Change-Id: Ib1b2a627e4dea24717e3ee907dc8a4cf82fc6e7f Signed-off-by: Mark Yao <mark.yao@rock-chips.com> Signed-off-by: Douglas Anderson <dianders@chromium.org> (cherry picked from git://people.freedesktop.org/~airlied/linux drm-next commit 44d0237a26395ac94160cf23f32769013b365590) Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/346305

UPSTREAM: cpufreq: dt: Include types.h from cpufreq-dt.h cpufreq-dt.h uses 'bool' data type but doesn't include types.h. It works fine for now as the files that include cpufreq-dt.h, also include types.h directly or indirectly. But, when a file includes cpufreq-dt.h without including types.h, we get a build error. Avoid such errors by including types.h in cpufreq-dt itself. Signed-off-by: Viresh Kumar <viresh.kumar@linaro.org> Signed-off-by: Rafael J. Wysocki <rafael.j.wysocki@intel.com> (cherry picked from commit 7e67e239a4f32fa3e2d51dd9a7930018651635b6) BUG=chrome-os-partner:53468 TEST=build and boot for kevin Change-Id: I11856300d5581364902e0f44dc3d40c4f8b0ec4d Signed-off-by: Brian Norris <briannorris@chromium.org> Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/346482 Reviewed-by: Douglas Anderson <dianders@chromium.org>

CHROMIUM: drm/rockchip: Force pending callbacks in vop_disable_plane() When the video_decode_accelerator_unittest is killed while running, a hung task panic can sometimes be triggered on Mali drivers. The drm driver waits for GPU jobs that have been reserved, but won't be run. This deadlock can be resolved by triggering pending callbacks before waiting. This issue is extremely similar to chrome-os-partner:51276. BUG=chromium:599783 TEST=Ran video_HangoutHardwarePerf.vp8 200 times on veyron_jerry and verified no reboots occurred. The command is: test_that --iterations 200 -b veyron_jerry <ip> video_HangoutHardwarePerf.vp8 Change-Id: I234a28e1240dce0899d31a5200538e87e6b793eb Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/346254 Commit-Ready: Gurchetan Singh <gurchetansingh@chromium.org> Tested-by: Gurchetan Singh <gurchetansingh@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Stéphane Marchesin <marcheu@chromium.org>
